name: linked-k24-gather-qvm-n-half
rationale: Reaching variant of linked-zero-k cases of this entry (DESIGN D296), whose parameters stop the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 32 lanes; the user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias; constant 122 binds a two-entry table (1 source, 1 destination). The parameters select N = 32 outputs (one threadgroup's 32 columns) over K = 24 rows: the guard (threadgroup_position.y << 5) < N passes, lanes 0 to 23 each dequantize one 8-bit row of W (row stride N bytes) and scale it, the simdgroup sums the 32 partial results, and lane 0 hands all 32 to the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at element indices 0 to 31 (128 bytes, observed whole). x holds 1, 2, 3 repeating, the scales 0.5, 1, 2 repeating, the biases 0 to 3 repeating, and W small integers below 16, so every product and partial sum is an integer multiple of 0.5 far below 2^24: exact in any order or contraction.

name: linked-zero-k-gather-qvm-n-half
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: A single invocation and unit gather batch select literal index zero from the authored buffers. The quantized K extent and vector-row count are zero while the quantization group size is one, making every accumulation and final postfix loop zero-trip and leaving the sole bounded destination element unchanged. Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: linked-single-threadgroup-zero-bin
rationale: One 1x1 threadgroup dispatches one invocation. kLogBinEntries=0 makes both initialization and flush loops contain exactly one bin, kTGSizeIs256=false uses the literal one-thread group size as their stride, and source_size=1x1 bounds the image path. The exact linked callback returns float4 zero without dereferencing resources; the poisoned global bin makes the local-atomic aggregation observable byte-exactly.

name: slide-a-five-layer-box-across-six-layers-with-both-edges-short
rationale: No authored case reached `llvm.smin.i16`, which six corpus sources use; this 166-line kernel is the smallest and calls it exactly once, in the denominator of its running box average, so the call's answer is visible in every output texel. The kernel slides a (2*boxRadius + 1)-layer box along the array axis of a 2d texture array, keeping a running sum: at step t it subtracts layer t - 2r - 1 when that layer exists, adds layer t when it exists, and at t >= r divides by the number of layers actually inside the box. That count is `(2r + 1) + select(t < arraySize, 0, arraySize - 1 - t) + smin(t - 2r, 0)`: the select shortens the box at the trailing edge and the `smin` shortens it at the leading edge. With boxRadius 2 over six layers the six written layers take the divisors 3, 4, 5, 5, 4 and 3 -- `smin` supplies the -2 and -1 of the first two and nothing after, the select supplies the -1 and -2 of the last two and nothing before -- so the two edge terms are separated from each other as well as from the constant 5. Signedness is the whole point of the call: `t - 2r` is -2 and -1 as an i16, which an unsigned minimum (or a maximum) reads as a huge positive and answers 0, making the first two divisors 5 and leaving the other four unchanged. The six input values per column are chosen so that every one of the six window sums is an exact multiple of its own divisor and the six quotients are distinct: column 0 holds 1, 2, 3, 6, 18, 21 and answers 2, 3, 6, 10, 12, 15; column 1 holds 4, 9, 8, 11, 13, 24 and answers 7, 8, 9, 13, 14, 16. All twelve inputs and all twelve answers are distinct, so a layer permuted, a column swapped, a window that started or ended one layer off, or a divisor taken from the wrong step all land on a value no correct texel holds. Every quotient is a small integer and equals its own reciprocal-multiplied form in f32, so `fdiv fast` cannot separate the two spellings here. The four channels carry the same layer value scaled by 1, 3, 9 and -1, which makes each texel's components mutually distinct (so a swizzle shows) and puts a negative through the same divide. The destination starts as 0xBE poison in all 192 bytes. Note the shader's own loop runs one step past the last in-range layer and writes at array index `arraySize`; Metal discards a write outside a texture's bounds, and that discarded write is the shader's behaviour, not something this case chooses. `execution_safety` is `authored_bounded`: the AIR loop is a real cycle whose trip count is `arraySize + boxRadius + 1`, which this case pins to 9.

name: map-physical-coordinates-through-rate-maps-an-argument-buffer-holds
rationale: Metal ground truth for rasterization-rate maps whose pointers an argument buffer holds (DESIGN D240), the placement two corpus rows read their maps from: the argument buffer at buffer 0 holds `coordinates` (byte 0, eight float2 inputs as plain bytes), `left` (byte 8) and `right` (byte 16), and grid row y = 0 maps through `left` and row y = 1 through `right`, the compiler selecting the member's address and then loading the pointer. Each map member is authored as `rasterization_rate_map`: the Metal oracle encodes a buffer of what copyParameterDataToBuffer:offset: writes for the map newRasterizationRateMapWithDescriptor: compiles, and a Vulkan executor one of this crate's parameter data of the same map (bind::RasterizationRateMap). `left` is a 64x64 map of uniform quality 1.0 (the identity) and `right` is 37x23 with horizontal samples [0.5, 1] and vertical samples [1, 0.5], the two maps whose tiles this crate compiles as Apple M3 does (DESIGN D235.8). The coordinates (0, 0), (1.5, 2.5), (10.25, 7.75), (17.5, 11.5), (20.125, 3.875), (31.25, 20.75), (35.5, 21.5), (5, 18) lie inside both physical extents (64x64 and 36x23) at exact binary fractions; through `right` seven of them move along x (this crate's decoder answers 1.546875, 10.5703125, 18.046875, 20.753906, 32.226563, 36.5, 5.15625) and y is the identity, so a map read from the wrong member, or Apple's bytes decoded as this crate's, cannot hide. Output: sixteen float2 (row-major lanes, x then y bits) into buffer 1.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-sixteen-dual-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 16 and receives exact float4 zero from all fifteen linked _uber_clear bodies. An eighteen-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. This entry swizzles it to float4(0,0,0,1), writes both required poisoned output textures, and captures binding zero byte-exactly.

name: read-query-null-test-and-write-argument-buffer-textures
rationale: Four threads use the textures of constant argument buffer 0 {texture2d<float> source; texture2d<float, access::write> target;} (the D38 heap: access.handle.lookup, texture.read.heap, texture.query.heap, texture.is_null.heap, texture.write.heap, DESIGN D162, D213). source, at field 0, is a 4x1 rgba32_float texture whose texel x is (x, 0.5x, -1, 2); target, at field 8, is a 4x1 rgba32_float storage texture, initially 0xab. Thread g writes source(g) + (source's width 4, is_null(source), 0, 0) at texel g of target. source is bound, so is_null is 0 (the case schema declares every argument-buffer texture the AIR reaches, so a null member is not expressible): target(g) = (g + 4, 0.5g, -1, 2). The observation is the whole of target. The AIR has no loop.

name: sample-and-query-an-argument-buffer-cube-and-count-a-cube-array
rationale: DESIGN D285.15: constant argument buffer 0 is {texturecube<float> sky; texturecube_array<float> skies;}. Thread g samples sky along axis g / 2, positive for an even g (+X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, -Z), with the constexpr nearest sampler at level 0, and writes (the sample's x, sky's mip level count, sky's width, skies' array size) to buffer 1. sky is a 2x2 rgba32_float cube whose face f holds (f + 1, 0, 0, 1) in all four texels, so the sample pins the face alone and no intra-face texel convention; skies is two 2x2 cubes (values never read). The engine queries sky through its sampled cube class and skies through the cube-array class, with no division by 6. Thread g writes (g + 1, 1, 2, 2).

name: unclamped-and-clamped-lod-of-a-texture-selected-per-quad
rationale: DESIGN D285.13: tail_select_unclamped_lod selects near (64x64, texture 0) for a fragment left of x = 8 and far (4x4, texture 1) otherwise, then asks the selected texture's unclamped and clamped LOD at c = position.xy / 16 through the constexpr sampler mip_linear. The engine queries both candidates before the switch-at-use, which selects the value. position's derivative across a quad is exactly one pixel and x = 8 lies between quads, so each quad reads one candidate and the scale in texels per pixel is size / 16: the unclamped LOD is log2(4) = 2 on the left half and log2(1/4) = -2 on the right, and the clamped LOD is 0 on both (single-level textures). Every pixel is (2, 0, 0, 1) left of x = 8 and (-2, 0, 0, 1) right of it; the texel values are never read.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-seven-2x1-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 27 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-six linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-nine-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The complete 2x1 primary block at origin (2,0) is captured byte-exactly from the poisoned 4x1 resource.

rationale: One 1x1 threadgroup dispatches one invocation. kLogBinEntries=0 makes both initialization and flush loops contain exactly one bin, kTGSizeIs256=false uses the literal one-thread group size as their stride, and source_size=1x1 bounds the image path. name: fast-cos-flushes-past-the-last-quadrant
rationale: The entry evaluates fast_cos(input.rg * pi/100 - pi) and maps it to (cos + 1) * 0.5. Texel 0 carries 3e8 and a quiet NaN, whose arguments are 9424775.0 and NaN: both are past the 6588397.5 quadrant boundary where Metal's fast::cos gives up and answers exactly 0.0, so both channels must read back 0.5. Texel 1 carries 100.0 twice, whose argument is exactly 0.0, so both channels must read back 1.0. Every observed value is either the flush constant or cos(0), so the case pins the flush boundary and the NaN arm without depending on any implementation's transcendental precision.

name: narrow-shuffles-and-quad-reductions-in-one-simdgroup
rationale: One 32-lane simdgroup reading itself through eight families the corpus calls but no case covered: simd_shuffle_down at half4 and at the three narrow integer widths (uchar, char, short), quad_sum at float3 and float2, and quad_shuffle_down at float3 and float2. The narrow integer slots pin the widths a lowering could silently promote: the char lane carries a negative value so a zero-extending shuffle is caught, and the short lane spans -2900..4600 so a truncation to a byte is too. The quad_sum lanes are reductions over four lanes, not shuffles, so they also pin that the reduction clusters to the quad and not to the simdgroup: every lane of a quad reads back its own quad's sum, and the four quad sums differ. Slots whose source lane leaves the group are overwritten with zero under a branch on tid -- Metal leaves those undefined -- so no lane asserts on undefined behaviour. The 545th word is left at the 0xABABABAB fill and read back as an overrun guard.

name: void-fragment-no-writes
rationale: The entry is structurally a single void return: it declares no color, depth, or stencil result members and marks both inputs unused. A real fragment draw must complete without any shader-writable observable bytes, so the exact output is the empty byte sequence.

name: fragment-alpha-float-to-half4-white
rationale: The fragment truncates its scalar float alpha varying to half and returns half4 (1,1,1,alpha); the generated fullscreen vertex stage supplies alpha and the complete pixel captures the conversion.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-eight-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 28 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-seven linked _uber_clear bodies. A thirty-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The entry writes that result to the poisoned primary texel before subgroup aggregation, and binding zero is captured byte-exactly.

name: unlock-atomic-word
rationale: One loop-free invocation uses thread_position_in_grid.x zero to select the sole four-byte atomic record and performs an exact global atomic store of zero over the complete poisoned word.
